newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says won't alter offer at WTO telecom talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan says won't alter offer at WTO telecom talks.

text.p: Japan will not offer to broaden its telecom liberalisation proposal to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) unless the United States agrees to do the same, a Japanese government official said on Friday.
Japan, the United States and 55 other countries in telecom talks at the WTO have until Saturday to reach agreement on liberalising the global telecommunications market.
"Japan will step up its efforts only in an environment in which all participants cooperate with each other," an official of the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said.
"We'll begin studies into what we can do if the U.S. itself makes a new proposal," he added, accusing the United States of "unilateralism".
A hard-line stance by the U.S. trade team has made participants sceptical that an accord can be reached by the deadline.

U.S. diplomats have threatened to withhold U.S. support for a deal unless other countries broaden their proposals for liberalisation, particularly regarding the permissible degree of foreign ownership, the ministry official said.

The official attacked the U.S. position, citing U.S. restrictions on direct foreign investment in U.S. wireless communications operators, adding that Japan had made the most advanced offer for liberalisation among the 57 participants.

In its WTO proposal, Japan pledged to lift all its restrictions on foreign ownership of telecommunications operators, including wireless businesses, except for industry giants Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD), which would retain a 20 percent foreign ownership limit.

The official said a letter from U.S. President Bill Clinton to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto urging Japan to include NTT and KDD in its liberalisation scheme would not alter the Japanese stance.
"Japan"s position remains unchanged," the official said.

Mitsuo Igarashi, vice minister for posts and telecommunications, made it clear in a recent news conference that there was no possibility that Japan would totally do away with foreign ownership restrictions on NTT and KDD.
